```{r, message = FALSE}
library(lavaan)
library(R2spa)
```

## Modeling change in a repeatedly measured construct

When a construct is measured by several indicators at each occasion,
researchers can model growth in the latent construct rather than growth
in an uncorrected composite. With 2S-PA, stage 1 estimates a longitudinal
measurement model and obtains a factor score for each occasion. Stage 2
fits a growth model while accounting for measurement error in those scores.

We use an example from Chapter 14 of *Growth Modeling* (Grimm, Ram, &
Estabrook, 2017), available in
[this tutorial](https://thechangelab.stanford.edu/tutorials/growth-modeling/measurement-invariance-2nd-order-growth-model/).
Science, reading, and mathematics scores at grades 3, 5, and 8 are used
as indicators of an academic achievement construct.

The example uses a **latent basis growth model**: the first and last slope
loadings are fixed at zero and one, and the middle loading is estimated.
It therefore permits a nonlinear pattern of mean change between the three
occasions rather than imposing a strictly linear time trend. The data are
stored with this vignette; the code below shows their original source.

```{r, echo = TRUE, eval = FALSE}
# Load data
eclsk <- read.table(
  "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/LRI-2/Data/main/GrowthModeling/ECLS_Science.dat",
  na.strings = "."
)
names(eclsk) <- c("id", "s_g3", "r_g3", "m_g3", "s_g5", "r_g5", "m_g5", "s_g8",
                  "r_g8", "m_g8", "st_g3", "rt_g3", "mt_g3", "st_g5", "rt_g5",
                  "mt_g5", "st_g8", "rt_g8", "mt_g8")
```

```{r, include = FALSE, eval = FALSE}
saveRDS(eclsk, file = "eclsk.rds")
```

```{r, include = FALSE}
eclsk <- readRDS("eclsk.rds")
```

## Joint SEM: measurement and growth estimated together

The tutorial first evaluates longitudinal measurement invariance and then
fits a growth model using a strict invariance specification. Equal
loadings and item intercepts establish a common measurement scale over
time; equal item residual variances add strict invariance. Residual
covariances between repeated measures of the same indicator are also
included. The joint SEM below estimates the measurement and growth
parameters simultaneously.

```{r}
jsem_growth_mod <- "
# factor loadings (with constraints)
eta1 =~ 15.1749088 * s_g3 + l2 * r_g3 +  l3 * m_g3
eta2 =~ 15.1749088 * s_g5 + l2 * r_g5 +  l3 * m_g5
eta3 =~ 15.1749088 * s_g8 + l2 * r_g8 +  l3 * m_g8

# factor variances
eta1 ~~ psi * eta1
eta2 ~~ psi * eta2
eta3 ~~ psi * eta3

# unique variances/covariances 
s_g3 ~~ u1 * s_g3 + s_g5 + s_g8
s_g5 ~~ u1 * s_g5 + s_g8
s_g8 ~~ u1 * s_g8
r_g3 ~~ u2 * r_g3 + r_g5 + r_g8
r_g5 ~~ u2 * r_g5 + r_g8
r_g8 ~~ u2 * r_g8
m_g3 ~~ u3 * m_g3 + m_g5 + m_g8
m_g5 ~~ u3 * m_g5 + m_g8
m_g8 ~~ u3 * m_g8

# observed variable intercepts
s_g3 ~ i1 * 1
s_g5 ~ i1 * 1
s_g8 ~ i1 * 1
r_g3 ~ i2 * 1
r_g5 ~ i2 * 1
r_g8 ~ i2 * 1
m_g3 ~ i3 * 1
m_g5 ~ i3 * 1
m_g8 ~ i3 * 1

# latent basis model
i =~ 1 * eta1 + 1 * eta2 + 1 * eta3
s =~ 0 * eta1 + start(.5) * eta2 + 1 * eta3

i ~~ start(.8) * i
s ~~ start(.5) * s
i ~~ start(0) * s

i ~ 0 * 1
s ~ 1
"
jsem_growth_fit <- lavaan(jsem_growth_mod,
                          data = eclsk,
                          meanstructure = TRUE,
                          estimator = "ML",
                          fixed.x = FALSE)
```

## Stage 1: longitudinal measurement model

For 2S-PA, first estimate the measurement model without the growth factors.
The occasion-specific factors have freely estimated covariances, while the
same measurement-invariance constraints are retained. `eta1` has mean zero
and variance one to establish the reference occasion's scale.

```{r}
strict_mod <- "
# factor loadings
eta1 =~ 15.1749088 * s_g3 + l2 * r_g3 + l3 * m_g3
eta2 =~ 15.1749088 * s_g5 + l2 * r_g5 + l3 * m_g5
eta3 =~ 15.1749088 * s_g8 + l2 * r_g8 + l3 * m_g8

# factor variances/covariances
eta1 ~~ 1 * eta1 + eta2 + eta3
eta2 ~~ eta2 + eta3
eta3 ~~ eta3

# unique variances/covariances
s_g3 ~~ u1 * s_g3 + s_g5 + s_g8
s_g5 ~~ u1 * s_g5 + s_g8
s_g8 ~~ u1 * s_g8
r_g3 ~~ u2 * r_g3 + r_g5 + r_g8
r_g5 ~~ u2 * r_g5 + r_g8
r_g8 ~~ u2 * r_g8
m_g3 ~~ u3 * m_g3 + m_g5 + m_g8
m_g5 ~~ u3 * m_g5 + m_g8
m_g8 ~~ u3 * m_g8

# latent variable intercepts
eta1 ~ 0 * 1
eta2 ~ 1
eta3 ~ 1

# observed variable intercepts
s_g3 ~ i1 * 1
s_g5 ~ i1 * 1
s_g8 ~ i1 * 1
r_g3 ~ i2 * 1
r_g5 ~ i2 * 1
r_g8 ~ i2 * 1
m_g3 ~ i3 * 1
m_g5 ~ i3 * 1
m_g8 ~ i3 * 1
"
```

```{r}
# Get factor scores
fs_dat <- get_fs(eclsk, model = strict_mod)
```

## Stage 2: growth model

The three occasion-specific latent variables now indicate an intercept
factor `i` and a change factor `s`. The mean of `s` represents expected
change from the first to the last occasion on the chosen latent scale.
The middle slope loading locates grade 5 relative to those endpoints.
The variances of `i` and `s` describe individual differences in initial
level and change, and their covariance describes the association between them.

```{r}
# Growth model
tspa_growth_mod <- "
i =~ 1 * eta1 + 1 * eta2 + 1 * eta3
s =~ 0 * eta1 + start(.5) * eta2 + 1 * eta3

# factor variances
eta1 ~~ psi * eta1
eta2 ~~ psi * eta2
eta3 ~~ psi * eta3

i ~~ start(.8) * i
s ~~ start(.5) * s
i ~~ start(0) * s

i ~ 1
s ~ 1
"
```

`tspa()` obtains the score loadings, error covariance, and intercepts from
`fs_dat`. These constraints connect the occasion scores to the latent
achievement variables before the growth model is estimated:

```{r}
tspa_growth_fit <- tspa(tspa_growth_mod, fs_dat, estimator = "ML")
```

## Comparison

The following tables show the growth-factor means, variances, and covariance.
The joint SEM fixes the intercept-factor mean to zero, whereas the stage-2
model estimates it; the mean specifications should therefore be considered
when comparing the output. The two approaches also differ in whether
measurement and growth parameters are estimated simultaneously or separately.

```{r}
parameterestimates(tspa_growth_fit) |>
  subset(subset = lhs %in% c("i", "s") & op %in% c("~1", "~~"))
parameterestimates(jsem_growth_fit) |>
  subset(subset = lhs %in% c("i", "s") & op  %in% c("~1", "~~"))
```
